MSFT.headline: Microsoft answers Trump's data center tax threat, but nothing in the model moves
paragraphs: Nothing in the last day and a half changes a model assumption. The newest item is Microsoft president Brad Smith on CBS's Face the Nation on Sunday, November 22, answering President Trump's Friday threat to penalize companies that build data centers abroad. Smith said most data centers have to sit close to the customers they serve, "You can't support Helsinki from New Jersey", and he announced no change to Microsoft's building plans. The threat still has no rate, order, bill or date, so it stays a risk to watch for capex, cost of revenue and overseas Intelligent Cloud revenue growth, not a number to change.

On the November 12 Microsoft 365 outage, Smith apologized, said it was not a cyberattack and not linked to AI, and said Microsoft has taken nine fixes with 13 more to come. He also said to be prepared "for the coming months", which is a mild caution for the resilience thesis. No customer credits or costs have been disclosed, so nothing goes through Productivity revenue growth or operating margin yet. The Nadella "perfect storm" headlines are loud but describe the same outage and add no figure.

The other high scoring stories are older news resurfacing. The ByteDance briefing request is the November 18 Reuters story, with no deal signed; GeekWire reports Smith expects Microsoft to answer the House committee's questions. The Intel agreement (multi-year Xeon supply and Intel packaging for Microsoft's own chips) was announced by both companies on November 18 with no dollar terms, so capex is unchanged. Secondary outlets say Anthropic's IPO filing shows a commitment of at least $47.2B to Azure through June 2033, which supports Intelligent Cloud revenue growth but was filed on November 10 and is not new.
watch: Any written order, bill or tax rate behind Trump's overseas data center threat
Microsoft's final outage review, and any customer credits or added resilience spending that would touch operating margin
The House China committee briefing on ByteDance, and whether the reported $500M Azure deal is signed or dropped
MSFT.note: Confirmed by Microsoft: Smith's remarks (CBS transcript, partly read), its outage cause reports, and the Intel agreement (joint release). Reported only: the ByteDance talks (The Information via Reuters and others, no company comment), Anthropic's Azure commitment (secondary summaries of its S-1, filing not opened), and the Rocket training system (NewsBytes); the CNBC Nadella articles, Barron's and 24/7 Wall St. pieces are headline only, articles not read.
